summary.text: A desktop, web and terminal workbench built around a shared TypeScript agent runtime.

maturity.text: Two public commits at this snapshot. The source opening exposes implementation, but not original feature dates.

advantages.text: A complete product stack lets students trace one runtime through several user surfaces.
The explicit turn loop and plugin manifest provide approachable TypeScript reading entrypoints.

tradeoffs.text: Public history cannot establish when the imported features were developed.
The notice says host tools run with the system account's permissions; permission controls do not provide default OS isolation.

taskFit.text: UI-rich local and remote coding workflows across desktop, web and terminal.
Studying product integration, plugin contracts and a TypeScript turn loop.

nodes.label: Agent runtime
nodes.subtitle: Shared TypeScript loop

responsibility.text: Drains runtime input, compacts context, initializes MCP and runs the next model-backed step.

nodes.inputs: User input, history and runtime configuration
nodes.extension: Desktop and web use shared RPC/client layers; the CLI enters the runtime directly.
nodes.failureMode: Long histories and queued steering require deliberate context handling.

nodes.label: Provider request
nodes.subtitle: Projected messages

responsibility.text: Projects the current context into messages for the configured model provider.

nodes.extension: Provider adapters form a separate integration seam.
nodes.failureMode: Provider errors interrupt sampling without implying a completed turn.

nodes.label: Tool scheduler
nodes.subtitle: Permission → execution

responsibility.text: Schedules model-requested tools and returns their results for the following model round.

nodes.extension: Tool handlers and MCP extend the callable operations.
nodes.failureMode: Tool failure and permission rejection require different handling.

nodes.label: SQLite sessions
nodes.subtitle: Messages and checkpoints

responsibility.text: Keeps CLI session data in SQLite, alongside product-specific persisted settings and runtime state.

nodes.extension: Other product surfaces own additional data and settings.
nodes.failureMode: Closing a window or uninstalling a client does not erase all local or remote copies.

nodes.label: Plugin manifest
nodes.subtitle: Skills · hooks · MCP

responsibility.text: A plugin groups agents, commands, skills, hooks, MCP servers and settings.

nodes.extension: The manifest exposes explicit component fields.
nodes.failureMode: Plugin admission and workspace-hook trust are separate decisions.

code.annotation: Selected manifest fields; unrelated fields omitted. The bundle can contribute several capability types.

nodes.label: Permission service
nodes.subtitle: Rules and workspace trust

responsibility.text: Controls tool permission and workspace hook trust under the selected operating mode.

nodes.failureMode: The notice warns that noninteractive prompt mode can default to yolo if no mode is supplied.

nodes.label: Host execution
nodes.subtitle: System account authority

responsibility.text: File, terminal and Git operations run with the execution host account's authority. The notice does not promise a default OS sandbox.

nodes.extension: External containment can be supplied by the environment.
nodes.failureMode: Permission approval must not be mistaken for operating-system containment.

chapters.title: The shared runtime
chapters.heading: One runtime, three surfaces
chapters.body: Desktop, web and terminal entrypoints meet a shared agent runtime.
chapters.takeaway: Separate the product's interface from the agent's execution loop.

chapters.title: From model to tools
chapters.heading: Follow the next action

chapters.takeaway: A model adapter changes the request boundary, not the whole product.

chapters.takeaway: The current notice is essential evidence for understanding the actual boundary.
